title: An Otherworldly Glow
caption: Green-lit ALMA antennas under the Milky Way, Chajnantor plateau, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at ALMA, Chajnantor plateau, Chile

recognition.text: ESO Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: The antennas of the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array seem to glow an eerie, vivid green in this photograph from the Chajnantor plateau, high in Chile's Atacama Desert. It could almost be a landing site for friendly aliens, but the explanation is ordinary: indicator lights on the antennas tell staff whether it is safe to approach, and green means yes.

Above them, the clear Chilean sky holds the band of the Milky Way. In the top left, two bright stars sit side by side. They are often called the Pointers, because they lead the eye to the bright diamond shape of the Southern Cross immediately to their right.

The one closer to the Southern Cross is Beta Centauri, some 400 light-years away. The other is Alpha Centauri, the nearest star system to the Sun at just 4.37 light-years. It includes the red dwarf Proxima Centauri, where in 2016 astronomers using ESO telescopes found evidence of an Earth-sized planet in the habitable zone.

understand.eye: The camera records the Milky Way far more vividly than the eye would see it.
